statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the following holds. Let a walk be a finite sequence of cells p_0,...,p_L inside the grid such that p_0=(0,0), p_L=(m-1,n-1), and for every t with 0 <= t < L the cells p_t and p_{t+1} are orthogonally adjacent (the sum of the absolute row difference and absolute column difference is 1). The obstacle count of the walk is the number of distinct cells (i,j) with 0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j]=1, and p_t=(i,j) for some t. The walk is feasible if its obstacle count is at most k. Then r is the minimum length L over all feasible walks if at least one feasible walk exists, and r = -1 if no feasible walk exists.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Preconditions: 1 <= m, n <= 40; every row of grid has length n; grid[i][j] is 0 or 1 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n; grid[0][0] = grid[m-1][n-1] = 0; and 0 <= k <= m*n.

statement: Under the preconditions, the function returns a result (Result.ok) for every valid input; it does not fail due to arithmetic overflow, out-of-bounds indexing, or panic. The returned value may be -1.

statement: For any two bounds k1 and k2 with 0 <= k1 <= k2 <= m*n, let r1 be the result of shortest_path(grid,k1) and r2 the result of shortest_path(grid,k2). Whenever both evaluations return results, if r1 != -1 then r2 != -1 and r2 <= r1.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Preconditions: 1 <= m, n <= 40; every row of grid has length n; grid[i][j] is 0 or 1 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n; grid[0][0] = grid[m-1][n-1] = 0; and 0 <= k1 <= k2 <= m*n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, every sequence p_0,...,p_r of cells inside the grid with p_0=(0,0), p_r=(m-1,n-1), and consecutive cells orthogonally adjacent has exactly (r + m + n - 2)/2 steps t for which (row(p_{t+1}) + col(p_{t+1})) - (row(p_t) + col(p_t)) = 1, and exactly (r - (m + n - 2))/2 steps t for which this difference is -1. Here row(p) and col(p) denote the row and column indices of cell p.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[0]). Preconditions: 1 <= m, n <= 40; every row of grid has length n; grid[i][j] is 0 or 1 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n; grid[0][0] = grid[m-1][n-1] = 0; and 0 <= k <= m*n.
